key_insight: A foundation-model-based, data-efficient pipeline can detect duodenal epithelial neoplasia from whole-slide biopsy images with strong cross-hospital performance.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help support histopathology workflows for rare duodenal tumours, where labelled training data are scarce.
method: Used haematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images from 5 hospitals, split into patches and encoded with the Hibou-B foundation model.
Compared global standardisation with unsupervised site-specific standardisation of patch embeddings.
Applied PCA, Gaussian mixture modelling, and a Random Forest classifier for detection.
evidence_signal: Across leave-one-hospital-out validation, performance was 90% accuracy with AUC 0.96, and on an external hospital test set it reached 94% accuracy with AUC 0.97.
watch_item: Results are promising but need prospective validation and workflow testing before real-world deployment, especially given the small number of neoplastic cases.
paper_title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study
